method: One independent reviewer generated concrete answers from prompts and installed-style library content before opening fixture assertions, implementation tests or upstream source, then manually graded the fixed answers. NPU fixture contains assertions are separately labeled structural checks.
selection: Each root, one synthetic case per each of eight subskills per repository, and both integrated cases per repository.

cases.semantic_assessment: Routes stack, profiling, data, compiler and distributed work with evidence prerequisites; separates newer TorchNPU and installed/source identities.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Routes installation identity, profiling, training/data and compiler before tuning a hypothesis.
Keeps PyTorch and TorchNPU source identities independent rather than asserting a compatible pair.
Distinguishes source inventory and installed CPU diagnostics from target backend evidence.
Uses bundled resources rather than requiring the original distillation checkout.

cases.semantic_assessment: Preserves existing environment, identifies current PEP517/scikit-build-core and forwarding rules, and withholds CUDA-extension success.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Separates CPU wheel/backend availability from a toolkit and from extension compilation.
Uses the current scikit-build-core/PEP517 recipe and forwarding rules rather than legacy setup.py build flags.
Chooses a new isolated build environment or reports missing prerequisites without mutating the existing one.
Withholds CUDA extension success until compilation and actual backend execution.

cases.semantic_assessment: Explains shared detached storage/version failure and shared jagged offsets, with small semantic/gradient checks and no blanket layout fix.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Explains detach can share storage and saved-version checks can fail.
Locates and removes or correctly stages the offending mutation rather than using .data.
Distinguishes equal jagged lengths from the required shared offsets constituent.
Uses bounded alias/gradient and ragged checks and does not claim every nested operator is supported.

cases.semantic_assessment: Starts zero-worker control, shards iterable by worker/rank, handles Windows spawn/persistence, fixes accumulation boundary and SDPA dropout/masks.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Starts with a zero-worker data/schema control and explicitly disables incompatible prefetch/persistent settings.
Shards the iterable across worker and rank replicas and accounts for spawn pickling.
Keeps a fixed scale through accumulation, unscales once after the full window, then clips/steps/updates.
Sets SDPA dropout_p to zero at eval and checks its Boolean mask semantics.

cases.semantic_assessment: Separates guards/breaks/compiler stages, fixes contradictory example and range, tests valid/invalid/roundtrip, and separates deployment and timings.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Distinguishes guard failure/recompilation from graph breaks and isolates eager, Dynamo eager, AOT eager, then target lowering.
Explains shape and Python state guards and avoids disabling guards to claim dynamic support.
Corrects example/range relations and checks valid plus invalid export shapes and roundtrip.
Separates export correctness from real deployment compatibility and measured cold/steady performance.

cases.semantic_assessment: Separates ordering and storage lifetime, joins result consumption, copies into static graph buffers and explains private-pool retention.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Separates wait_stream ordering from record_stream allocator lifetime.
Orders producer-to-consumer and result consumption and keeps in-flight storage alive.
Copies new values into static captured input storage instead of rebinding a Python variable.
Explains graph-private pool reservation versus live allocation and withholds unavailable CUDA runtime success.

cases.semantic_assessment: Rejects untrusted DCP conversion, initializes target sharding/optimizer/hooks correctly, and starts hang analysis at first rank divergence.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Explicitly states DCP/conversion does not inherit torch.load weights_only protections and requires trusted infrastructure-produced storage.
Constructs optimizer after fully_shard and calls model(x) so unshard hooks fire.
Allocates target sharded state and validates keys/layout/topology before DCP load.
Starts with first rank exception and collective-order/signature ledger; does not fix a mismatch just by extending timeout.

cases.semantic_assessment: Distinguishes absent events from absent GPU work, accounts for profiler retention, and defines replicated synchronized timing with limited claims.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Checks actual backend/profiler activities and capture window rather than assuming absent GPU work.
Explains shape/stack profiler reference retention and overhead.
Synchronizes the intended completion boundary and uses controlled replicated timing with separate cold compile.
Limits the conclusion to the measured scope and requires separate service evidence for a service claim.

cases.semantic_assessment: Correctly distinguishes mutation/output alias, metadata/fake, registration/numerical gradient checks and native backward stride/stream obligations.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Distinguishes output alias contract from mutation metadata and returns fresh output or correct supported schema.
Matches fake size/stride/dtype/device metadata without reading data.
Explains opcheck registration/functionalization and gradcheck derivative mathematics are separate.
Handles incoming gradient strides explicitly and requires target device/stream checks for the native kernel.

cases.semantic_assessment: Composes state, rank/data partition, accumulation, compiler isolation and first-error diagnosis before numerical or throughput claims.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Covers distributed/checkpoint, training/data, compiler and profiling routes with explicit state/rank/shape contracts.
Restores optimizer/scaler/RNG/data progress as required and allocates intended sharded state.
Checks effective-batch scale/clipping and equal collective order on uneven rank work.
Keeps numerical correctness and actual device/multi-rank verification separate from compilation and throughput claims.

cases.semantic_assessment: Composes attention semantics, custom-op contracts, real CUDA lifetime checks, export range and separately qualified ONNX consumer.

fixture_assertion_results.assertion: Connects custom-op schema/fake/autograd, attention semantics, stream/capture lifetime and export routes.
Requires fake metadata without data reads and checks SDPA mask/dropout contracts.
Keeps static captured buffer addresses with copy-in and actual CUDA checks.
Qualifies ONNX translation/opset/external weights and target execution separately; preserves missing backend blockers.

cases.semantic_assessment: Gives staged install/device/graph/memory/HCCL/training/profiling routes and names unavailable device checks explicitly.
Separates released row and source build line, explains TORCH_VERSION/build identity and isolated prerequisites without mutating the working stack.
Uses a fresh process, checks unloaded compiler modules without importing them, and separates registration, lazy device init and compile entry.
Defines broadcast output/Meta and per-input reduced gradients, separates dispatcher keys, preserves validation and defers target execution.
Provides producer/consumer and return edges, independent lifetime retention and explicit CPU completion boundary with an ownership ledger.
Rejects compilation inference from missing-TorchAir eager fallback and distinguishes graph-tree, optional EX, Inductor and FXRT paths.
Separates early future completion, work/consumer ordering, allocator protection and host completion, including a concrete two-rank helper command.
Keeps fixed scale over four normalized microbatches, unscales/clips/steps/updates at the effective boundary and observes disabled/overflow state.
Names shape/memory/stack-or-module prerequisites, active stepping, and separate collection/analysis/artifact/consumer statuses.
Describes captured fork/join, fixed branch input addresses, copy-in, output preservation and pending-event/private-pool reservation before timing.
Keeps HCCL, scaler and profiler state machines separate and retains all unavailable NPU and multi-rank checks on the CPU host.

limits: Textual procedure execution only; proposed commands and target backends were not executed in this usability pass.
Not a baseline-versus-skill trial, blind multi-reviewer study, model-quality assessment or evidence of empirical effectiveness.
TorchNPU assertions check source-file phrases; they are not automatic grading of generated answers. The separate semantic_status records this reviewer's manual answer assessment.
Required CUDA/NPU/HCCL, source-build, deployment-consumer and performance validation remains blocked or not_run as declared by the candidate graphs.
